# Setup

```{r}
#| label: load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(cmdstanr)
library(emmeans)
library(easystats)
library(modelbased)
library(tidybayes)
library(patchwork)
library(knitr)
library(here)

options(
  scipen = 999,
  marginaleffects_posterior_center = mean,
  brms.short_summary = TRUE,
  rms.backend = Sys.getenv("BRMS_BACKEND", "cmdstanr"),
  brms.threads = as.numeric(Sys.getenv("BRMS_THREADS", 2)),
  mc.cores = as.numeric(Sys.getenv("MAX_CORES", 4))
)
```

Shared preprocessing lives in `Scripts/data_prep.R` so the AI and DI documents can't drift out of sync on exclusion criteria. This produces `explicit_di` (and `explicit_ai`, unused here). Paths use `here::here()`, resolved from the project root, so this works regardless of which directory actually renders the document.

```{r}
#| label: data
source(here("Scripts", "data_prep.R"))
head(explicit_di)
```

# Model Specification

Same model class as `ddm-ai.qmd`: a hierarchical Bayesian drift diffusion model (Wiener process; Ratcliff, 1978) fit with `brms` (Bürkner, 2017) via Stan (Carpenter et al., 2017), sampled with `cmdstanr`, decomposing each trial's response time and choice into **drift rate** (`mu`), **non-decision time** (`ndt`), **starting point** (`bias`), and **boundary separation** (`bs`).

## Fixed and random effects

Identical structure to the AI document: `mu`, `ndt`, and `bias` each get the full `condition * dist * age.group` factorial structure (`0 +` cell-means coding on `condition`); `bs` is a single freely-varying parameter with no predictors; by-subject random intercept and `dist` slope on `mu` only (`(1 + dist | p | sn)`) — see `ddm-ai.qmd` for why random effects on `ndt`/`bias` were ruled out (identifiability, given how few trials exist per subject per cell).

```{r}
#| label: formula
formula_di <- bf(
  duration | dec(dec_recode) ~ 0 + condition + dist + age.group +
    condition:dist + condition:age.group + dist:age.group +
    condition:dist:age.group +
    (1 + dist | p | sn),
  ndt ~ 0 + condition + dist + age.group +
    condition:dist + condition:age.group + dist:age.group +
    condition:dist:age.group,
  bias ~ 0 + condition + dist + age.group +
    condition:dist + condition:age.group + dist:age.group +
    condition:dist:age.group
)
```

## Link functions

Same as AI: `mu` identity, `ndt` identity (bounded via prior, not link), `bias` logit (constrains to (0,1)), `bs` identity (Stan constrains it positive at the parameter-declaration level regardless of link).

```{r}
#| label: family
family_di <- wiener(link_bs = "identity", link_ndt = "identity", link_bias = "logit")
```

## Priors

```{r}
#| label: prior
bprior_di <-
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = b) +                                      # drift rate (mu) fixed effects
  prior(normal(0.3, 0.1), class = b, dpar = ndt, lb = 0, ub = "min_Y") + # ndt fixed effects
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = b, dpar = bias) +                         # bias, logit scale: 0.5 <-> logit 0
  prior(normal(0, 0.03), class = sd, group = sn, lb = 0)                # by-subject random effects (mu)
```

```{r}
#| label: prior-table
bprior_di |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::select(prior, class, dpar, group, lb, ub) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(everything(), ~ dplyr::na_if(as.character(.x), ""))) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Priors specified for the DI-group model.")
```

`bs` has no prior line above (see `ddm-ai.qmd`'s equivalent note) — it falls under `class = Intercept, dpar = bs` and rides on `brms`'s default.

```{r}
#| label: init
tmp_dat_di <- make_standata(formula_di,
  family = family_di,
  data = explicit_di, prior = bprior_di
)

initfun_di <- function() {
  list(
    b = rnorm(tmp_dat_di$K, 0, 0.2),
    b_bs = .5,
    b_ndt = runif(tmp_dat_di$K_ndt, 0.001, 0.05),
    b_bias = rnorm(tmp_dat_di$K_bias, 0, 0.1),
    sd_1 = runif(tmp_dat_di$M_1, 0.05, 0.1),
    z_1 = matrix(rnorm(tmp_dat_di$M_1 * tmp_dat_di$N_1, 0, 0.01), tmp_dat_di$M_1, tmp_dat_di$N_1),
    L_1 = diag(tmp_dat_di$M_1)
  )
}
```

## Estimation

```{r}
#| label: sampler-settings
n_chains <- 4
n_iter <- 10000
n_warmup <- 500
n_thin <- 10
adapt_delta_val <- .95
max_treedepth_val <- 15
n_postwarmup_draws <- (n_iter - n_warmup) / n_thin * n_chains
```

The model was fit with `r n_chains` MCMC chains of `r n_iter` iterations each (`r n_warmup` warmup), thinned by `r n_thin`, yielding `r n_postwarmup_draws` post-warmup draws. `adapt_delta` = `r adapt_delta_val`, `max_treedepth` = `r max_treedepth_val`.

Cached in `analysis/models/`, resolved via `here()` (see `ddm-ai.qmd` for why, not a relative path). Split `.rds` parts (see `Scripts/split_rds.R`) are recombined before loading, if any exist.

```{r}
#| label: recombine-split-models
source(here("Scripts", "split_rds.R"))
check_and_combine_rds(here("analysis", "models"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fit
fit_di <- brm(formula_di,
  data = explicit_di,
  family = family_di,
  prior = bprior_di, init = initfun_di,
  chains = n_chains, cores = n_chains,
  iter = n_iter, warmup = n_warmup, sample_prior = TRUE,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE), thin = n_thin,
  file = here("analysis", "models", "di_3way_full"),
  control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta_val, max_treedepth = max_treedepth_val),
  backend = "cmdstanr", threads = threading(2)
)
```

## Credibility Criterion

Same as `ddm-ai.qmd`: contrasts are judged credible based on the 95% credible interval excluding zero together with `pd > 97.5%`. ROPE percentages are computed (each parameter gets its own scaled range — see the `rope-ranges` chunk under Extract Results) and available for supplementary context, but are not the basis for calling an effect credible here.

## Convergence check

```{r}
#| label: convergence
summary(fit_di)

ll_di <- log_lik(fit_di)
bad_idx <- which(!is.finite(ll_di), arr.ind = TRUE)
if (nrow(bad_idx) == 0) {
  message("no non-finite log-likelihood entries")
} else {
  bad_obs <- sort(unique(bad_idx[, "col"]))
  message(nrow(bad_idx), " non-finite entries across ", length(bad_obs), " observation(s)")
  explicit_di[bad_obs, c("sn", "condition", "dist", "age.group", "duration", "dec_recode")]
}
```

# Extract results (modelbased)

Everything the write-up below quotes comes from these objects — re-run this chunk after refitting and the prose updates itself.

```{r}
#| label: rope-ranges
rope_scale <- function(fit, dpar) {
  draws <- posterior_epred(fit, dpar = dpar)
  0.1 * sd(as.vector(draws))
}

rope_mu <- rope_scale(fit_di, "mu")
rope_ndt <- rope_scale(fit_di, "ndt")
rope_bias <- rope_scale(fit_di, "bias")

c(mu = rope_mu, ndt = rope_ndt, bias = rope_bias)
```

`estimate_contrasts()` doesn't guarantee which level lands in `Level1` vs `Level2` — for this DI fit it assigned `Level1 = "uneq", Level2 = "eq"` (the opposite of the AI document's `Level1 = "eq", Level2 = "uneq"`), confirmed against raw `emmeans::pairs()` on the same cell (same magnitude, opposite sign, because the labels are swapped, not because the estimate differs). Every downstream number and every sentence in this document assumes `eq - uneq`, so normalize to that convention right here, once, rather than trying to remember which way each object happens to be oriented.

```{r}
#| label: normalize-direction
# Force every contrasts_* object below to report eq - uneq, regardless of
# which order estimate_contrasts() happened to assign Level1/Level2.
normalize_eq_minus_uneq <- function(df) {
  flip <- df$Level1 == "uneq"
  if (any(flip)) {
    new_low <- -df$CI_high[flip]
    new_high <- -df$CI_low[flip]
    df$Difference[flip] <- -df$Difference[flip]
    df$CI_low[flip] <- new_low
    df$CI_high[flip] <- new_high
    tmp <- df$Level1[flip]
    df$Level1[flip] <- df$Level2[flip]
    df$Level2[flip] <- tmp
    # pd and ROPE_Percentage are both symmetric around 0 and unaffected by the flip
  }
  df
}
```

```{r}
#| label: contrasts
contrasts_mu_di <- estimate_contrasts(
  fit_di, contrast = "dist", by = c("condition", "age.group"),
  predict = "mu", backend = "emmeans", rope_range = c(-rope_mu, rope_mu)
) |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()

contrasts_ndt_di <- estimate_contrasts(
  fit_di, contrast = "dist", by = c("condition", "age.group"),
  predict = "ndt", backend = "emmeans", rope_range = c(-rope_ndt, rope_ndt)
) |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()

contrasts_bias_di <- estimate_contrasts(
  fit_di, contrast = "dist", by = c("condition", "age.group"),
  predict = "bias", backend = "emmeans", rope_range = c(-rope_bias, rope_bias)
) |> normalize_eq_minus_uneq()

bias_by_condition_di <- estimate_means(
  fit_di, by = "condition", predict = "bias", backend = "emmeans"
)

contrasts_mu_di
contrasts_ndt_di
contrasts_bias_di
bias_by_condition_di
```

Check these column names before trusting the formatting helpers below — same caveat as the AI document.

```{r}
#| label: check-columns
names(contrasts_mu_di)
names(bias_by_condition_di)
```

```{r}
#| label: formatters
filter_row <- function(df, ...) {
  filters <- list(...)
  row <- df
  for (col in names(filters)) row <- row[row[[col]] == filters[[col]], ]
  if (nrow(row) != 1) stop("filter matched ", nrow(row), " rows, expected 1")
  row
}

fmt_contrast <- function(df, ...) {
  row <- filter_row(df, ...)
  sprintf(
    "%s, 95%% CI [%s, %s], *pd* = %s%%",
    insight::format_value(row$Difference),
    insight::format_value(row$CI_low),
    insight::format_value(row$CI_high),
    insight::format_value(row$pd * 100, digits = 1)
  )
}

fmt_mean <- function(df, ...) {
  row <- filter_row(df, ...)
  # estimate_means() names the value column after the dpar (e.g. "Bias"), not "Mean"
  value_col <- setdiff(names(df), c(names(list(...)), "CI_low", "CI_high", "pd", "ROPE_Percentage"))
  sprintf("%s, 95%% CI [%s, %s]", insight::format_value(row[[value_col]]), insight::format_value(row$CI_low), insight::format_value(row$CI_high))
}

# Primary credibility criterion (see ddm-ai.qmd): 95% CrI excludes zero AND
# pd > 97.5%. ROPE is not the basis for this.
credible_label <- function(df, ..., pd_threshold = 0.975) {
  row <- filter_row(df, ...)
  ci_excludes_zero <- (row$CI_low > 0) || (row$CI_high < 0)
  if (ci_excludes_zero && row$pd > pd_threshold) "credible" else "not credible"
}

# Three-way ROPE classification -- kept for supplementary context, not the
# primary credibility criterion (that's credible_label() above). See ddm-ai.qmd.
practical_label <- function(df, ..., lower = 0.05, upper = 0.95) {
  row <- filter_row(df, ...)
  if (row$ROPE_Percentage <= lower) {
    "practically meaningful"
  } else if (row$ROPE_Percentage > upper) {
    "negligible"
  } else {
    "ambiguous"
  }
}

fmt_rope <- function(df, ...) {
  row <- filter_row(df, ...)
  paste0(insight::format_value(row$ROPE_Percentage * 100, digits = 1), "%")
}
```

# Results

### Drift Rate

For 4–5-year-olds, the equal–unequal difference in drift rate was `r credible_label(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "4&5")` in the autonomous condition (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "4&5")`), `r credible_label(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "4&5")` in baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "4&5")`), and `r credible_label(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "4&5")` in norm (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "4&5")`).

By 6–7 years: autonomous (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "6&7")`), baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "6&7")`), norm (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "6&7")`).

By 8–9 years: autonomous (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "8&9")`), baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "8&9")`), norm (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "8&9")`).

Plotted together with `ndt` and `bias` at the end of the Results section (one combined figure via `patchwork`) rather than as three separate figures.

```{r}
#| label: fig-mu
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5
draws_mu_di <- pairs(emmeans(fit_di, ~ dist | condition * age.group, dpar = "mu")) |>
  gather_emmeans_draws()

p_mu_di <- ggplot(draws_mu_di, aes(x = .value, y = condition, fill = condition)) +
  stat_halfeye() +
  facet_wrap(~age.group) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Difference in drift rate (eq - uneq)", y = "Condition", title = "Drift rate (mu)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14)
```

### Non-Decision Time

For 4–5-year-olds: autonomous (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "4&5")`), baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "4&5")`), norm (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "4&5")`).

For 6–7-year-olds: autonomous (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "6&7")`), baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "6&7")`), norm (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "6&7")`).

For 8–9-year-olds: autonomous (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "8&9")`), baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "8&9")`), norm (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "8&9")`).

```{r}

draws_ndt_di <- pairs(emmeans(fit_di, ~ dist | condition * age.group, dpar = "ndt")) |>

p_ndt_di <- ggplot(draws_ndt_di, aes(x = .value, y = condition, fill = condition)) +
```

### Starting Point (Bias)

Bias got the same full `condition * dist * age.group` structure as `mu`/`ndt`. `contrasts_bias_di` (via `modelbased`) is on the response (0-1 probability) scale by default — see `ddm-ai.qmd` for how that was verified against `regrid("response")` — so the plot below matches it by using `regrid("response")` before `pairs()` rather than the logit scale.

For 4–5-year-olds, the equal–unequal difference in bias was `r credible_label(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "4&5")` in the autonomous condition (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "4&5")`), `r credible_label(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "4&5")` in baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "4&5")`), and `r credible_label(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "4&5")` in norm (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "4&5")`).

By 6–7 years: autonomous (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "6&7")`), baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "6&7")`), norm (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "6&7")`).

By 8–9 years: autonomous (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "8&9")`), baseline (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "8&9")`), norm (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_bias_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "8&9")`).


## Summary

```{r}
#| label: summary-helper
# how many of the 9 condition x age.group cells clear the credibility bar
# (pd) vs. the practical-significance bar (ROPE, <=5% overlap) -- these can
# and do diverge (see ddm-ai.qmd's NDT section: pd said "credible" almost
# everywhere, ROPE said "practically meaningful" in far fewer cells)
# Credible = 95% CrI excludes zero AND pd > 97.5% (same joint criterion as
# credible_label() above). ROPE-based counts kept for supplementary context.
count_credible <- function(df, pd_threshold = 0.975) {
  sum((df$CI_low > 0 | df$CI_high < 0) & df$pd > pd_threshold)
}
count_practical <- function(df, lower = 0.05) sum(df$ROPE_Percentage <= lower)
count_negligible <- function(df, upper = 0.95) sum(df$ROPE_Percentage > upper)
count_ambiguous <- function(df, lower = 0.05, upper = 0.95) sum(df$ROPE_Percentage > lower & df$ROPE_Percentage <= upper)
```

Reproducible tally across the 9 `condition x age.group` cells. Credibility (95% CrI excludes zero and `pd > 97.5%`) is the primary criterion; the ROPE-based breakdown is reported for supplementary context only (see Model Specification):

- drift rate: credible in `r count_credible(contrasts_mu_di)` of 9 cells
- non-decision time: credible in `r count_credible(contrasts_ndt_di)` of 9 cells
- bias's `dist` contrast: credible in `r count_credible(contrasts_bias_di)` of 9 cells

Marginal bias by condition: autonomous `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "autonomous")`, baseline `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "baseline")`, norm `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "norm")`.

**Confirmed: DI does not replicate AI's norm-specific pattern.** Drift rate is credible in all 9 of 9 `condition x age.group` cells — from the youngest age tested (4–5y: autonomous `r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "4&5")`, baseline `r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "4&5")`, norm `r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "4&5")`), regardless of prompt condition. This matches the paper's own finding (the Prompt x Allocation x Age interaction was dropped for Disadvantageous Inequity because it didn't improve model fit) and the earlier pre-`bias` exploratory signal in this project. If anything, `norm` is *not* the largest effect here the way it is in AI — at 6–7y it's the smallest of the three (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "norm", age.group = "6&7")` vs. baseline `r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "6&7")` and autonomous `r fmt_contrast(contrasts_mu_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "6&7")`), the opposite ordering from AI where norm led every age group.

**NDT is credible in all 9 of 9 cells, but grows fastest in baseline.** Same pattern as AI: `ndt`'s equal-vs-unequal difference is credible everywhere (`r count_credible(contrasts_ndt_di)` of 9 cells), including autonomous's smallest effect at 4–5y (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "4&5")`). What differs is magnitude: baseline grows fastest with age (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "baseline", age.group = "8&9")` by 8–9y), autonomous stays comparatively small throughout (`r fmt_contrast(contrasts_ndt_di, condition = "autonomous", age.group = "8&9")` even at 8–9y) — the same qualitative asymmetry as AI (autonomous's NDT effect is real but small relative to baseline/norm), just without any cell failing to clear the credibility bar at all here, unlike some of AI's youngest-age cells for `mu`.

**Bias tells the same story as AI.** Credible in only `r count_credible(contrasts_bias_di)` of 9 cells and practically meaningful in `r count_practical(contrasts_bias_di)` of 9, with no coherent age or condition trend — consistent with residual model flexibility rather than a real starting-point effect, same conclusion as the AI document. Marginal bias by condition doesn't differ credibly between conditions either (autonomous `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "autonomous")`, baseline `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "baseline")`, norm `r fmt_mean(bias_by_condition_di, condition = "norm")` — norm's interval overlaps the other two).

**Net conclusion**: disadvantageous inequity aversion is present from the youngest age tested and largely *independent* of experimental framing — children reject disadvantageous offers whether or not they're prompted to be fair, whether or not they're told to do whatever they want, or told nothing at all. This is the mirror image of the AI document's conclusion, where the fairness prompt was *necessary* to unlock early, credible inequity aversion. Read together, the two documents reproduce the source paper's central asymmetry — normative framing shapes children's willingness to reject advantageous (self-benefiting) unfairness, but disadvantageous inequity aversion doesn't need that kind of external prompting to show up early — and locate that asymmetry specifically in the evidence-accumulation process (drift rate), not in non-decision time or starting point, in both inequity conditions.
